title: An early 40.32-day GJ 176 residual wave raises later HARPS error in a fixed two-wave test
abstract: We search 71 early GJ 176 HARPS velocities for an extra stable sine wave after fixed terms for the known 8.776-day planet and 39.34-day rotation signal. The strongest grid peak from 2 to 200 days is at 40.31879 days. Its fixed early wave raises weighted squared error by 14.03 percent in 46 later visits across the instrument change. All 23 specified controls retain an error increase. A local period fit gives a 11.98 percent increase. Early full-search block-sign tail fractions range from 0.006 to 0.060. Late conditional score ranges depend on bin length and omit early fit uncertainty. A single free rotation wave also fails to transfer. Changing activity or an instrument response can explain the failure, but no cause is established. Recovery tests have low power at some periods. No new planet or independent observation is reported. The package gives the full small input, exact source hash, code, figures, controls and offline repeat steps.
